root.description: The id of the root the path is under

path.description: The routed file, relative to its root

anyOf.description: A content key: "<parserKind>.<keyKind>.<hex>" (keyKind sha256 | git-sha1 | git-sha256)

blob.description: The content key of the bytes, or null when the run holds none

variant.description: How the bytes were parsed: `json` strict (no comments, no trailing commas), `jsonc` with comments and trailing commas, `yaml` as a YAML 1.2 stream under the core schema (every document, aliases expanded, `<<` a plain key), `ini` an `.npmrc` read by npm's `ini` package as one object holding only its allowlisted top-level keys (every other key and every section dropped), `yarnrc` a `.yarnrc.yml` read as `yaml` and kept only through its key allowlist, every auth key (`npmAuthToken`, `npmAuthIdent`) dropped at any depth

state.description: `facts`: the pair's rows are held; `defective`: the bytes or the file decide it (malformed, not text, a lone surrogate, a `%YAML` version other than 1.2, a cap the bytes decide, a read the filesystem refused or failed), so the same file fails the same way every run: fix the file or exclude it in resources.extractors.data; `refused`: this run decided it (a time, heap or stack cap, a worker death, bytes changed or gone under the run, the machine out of descriptors or the path busy), so a rerun may answer, except a pair refused because a store-off run holds as many bytes of rows as it may: a rerun refuses it again, so run with the projection store on, inside a git repository

code.description: Why the pair is not `facts`, or null when it is

projection-data--routes.description: A row of the derived `data__routes` relation
